colours._how_to_read: hex = rendered sRGB in the best-lit plain patch. The renders are graded warm: the white radiator renders #d0baa0 in the daylight view, so hex_white_balanced applies the per-channel linear gains that make that radiator neutral (R x0.78, G x1.00, B x1.40). Use hex_white_balanced as a starting base colour under ~3000 K lights, or hex under neutral light. The night views (p03-p05) are warmer still.

light_colour_temperature.value: artificial light warm white, about 2700-3000 K (LED strips render #eed7aa to #f0e4d6, the lamp diffuser near white); daylight in p02 (and sun streaks on the door in p01) is neutral, sky #eaeff3; p03-p05 are lit by the warm interior lights only
light_colour_temperature.from: LED strip, diffuser and sky pixels in p02 and p04

notes: CEILING HEIGHT CONFLICT: with square pixels and the plan's horizontal dimensions, the renders put the ceiling at 2.61 m (joint fit; each render alone gives 2.56-2.62), not the owner's 2.40 m. Forcing 2.40 m needs a 9% vertical pixel stretch and fits worse (1.38 vs 1.06 px rms). It would also make the TV 1.10 x 0.59 m, which is not a TV shape, and put the door leaf top at 1.91 m. The 2.61 m reading gives a 1.10 x 0.64 m TV (a normal 50 inch) and a 2.07 m leaf top. So the render model is about 2.6 m tall, and all heights in this file are in that render-model scale.
The door leaf top measures 2.075 m (casing top 2.137), not the 2.00 m assumed. Forcing 2.00 would imply a 2.51 m ceiling, which also disagrees with 2.40.

Adapting to 2.40 m (owner decision needed): either keep absolute heights for things with real-world sizes (desk 0.80, sill 1.02, radiator, TV 1.41-2.05, handles, door) and re-anchor the ceiling-hung items to 2.40 (wardrobe top panel, tall unit, bookshelf, walnut panels and LED strips, track rails, curtain rod), or scale every y by 2.40/2.608 = 0.920. Window head 2.20, box top 2.40 and rod 2.49 cannot all fit under a 2.40 ceiling, so the window head, box and rod need a decision.

Validation opening p2-A ('window?' at x 0-0.46 on the top wall) is the bookshelf back, not a window. p2-C and p2-E (right wall) are the walnut panels with LED cavities, not windows. p2-D (left wall) is the TV, not a radiator. p2-B (radiator) and p2-F (door) are confirmed.

Three of the five cameras are outside the room (p01 beyond the right wall, p04 beyond the window wall, p05 beyond the left wall). Reproduce them with camera.near set to near_clip_m, or by hiding the wall behind the camera.

Camera accuracy: the joint fit (shared focal 1965 px, hfov 66.2 deg, vfov 52.1 deg) and a variant with a focal length per camera agree within 5 cm in position and 0.3 deg in angle. Edge reprojection rms is 0.5-1.5 px. Pitch is -2 to -4 deg (not zero); roll is under 0.1 deg. If the scene is built with a 2.40 m ceiling, keep the camera heights (1.38-1.49 m) as heights above the floor.
The desk height of 0.80 m comes from the joint fit (+-0.01). It is a height-adjustable desk, so this is only the setting shown.
The window frame's depth in the wall reveal and its exact right edge could not be measured; the x extent uses the plan sill line 0.46-1.93. With equal sashes the frame would end near 1.89.
Track rail B's far end, and whether rail A is one 3.2 m rail or two sections, could not be determined.
Colours are rendered pixel values under warm lighting; see colours._how_to_read.
Bookshelf boards and the closed base are greige, not walnut; walnut is the back panel and the central vertical divider.
